categories.title: Learning Workshops
categories.description: Hands-on Sainj Valley field courses for navigation, wilderness awareness, survival systems, teamwork, and low-impact travel habits.
details: Best for schools, colleges, creator cohorts, corporate learning groups, and beginners who want structured outdoor confidence before harder routes.
Modules combine map reading, compass use, route planning, shelter building, fire craft, water purification, emergency signalling, and Leave No Trace practice.
Programs include workshop manuals, technical equipment, certified team support, first-aid and safety cover, and flexible custom dates.

categories.title: Trekking Packages
categories.description: Post-monsoon Himalayan treks with clear pickup/drop logistics, team-size limits, priced departures, packing guidance, and field support.
details: Built for groups who want a defined itinerary, transparent inclusions, and real mountain route support rather than vague brochure copy.
Packages include route briefings, stay planning, meals on trek, local crew coordination, safety checks, and weather-aware pacing.
Difficulty ranges from easy-moderate Sainj Valley walks to moderate-difficult crossover and GHNP core-zone objectives.

categories.title: Custom Experiences
categories.description: Private programs built around your group profile, budget, dates, comfort level, learning goals, and terrain appetite.
details: Good for family trips, WFH cohorts, corporate offsites, creator-led communities, wellness hosts, and outdoor learning retreats.
KEAS can combine trekking, rock craft, wilderness skills, ecology walks, village stays, wellness practices, and content-friendly travel windows.

experiences.title: Into The Wild
experiences.summary: A hands-on wilderness immersion in Sainj Valley designed to help participants disconnect from comfort and reconnect with nature while learning practical mountain survival skills.
exclusions: Travel to/from pickup point unless specified
itinerary: Day 1: Aut pickup, arrival at KEAS base, wilderness briefing, gear orientation, group roles, and low-impact camp discipline.
Day 2: Shelter building, knot basics, fire-making methods, safe stove use, and evening reflection circle.
Day 3: Water sourcing, filtration and purification, emergency signalling, basic wilderness first aid, and team problem-solving drills.
Day 4: Jungle navigation, river-crossing basics, route choice, leadership rotation, and Leave No Trace field practice.
Day 5: Scenario-based survival challenge, debrief, personal preparedness plan, and drop at Aut.

experiences.title: The Art of Navigation
experiences.location: Sainj Valley forest, meadow and open alpine terrain
experiences.summary: A map, compass, and route-planning workshop for participants who want confidence in independent wilderness navigation across forest, meadow, and alpine terrain.
itinerary: Day 1: Aut pickup, Sainj orientation, navigation mindset, map symbols, scale, contour lines, and route-safety briefing.
Day 2: Compass handling, bearings, back-bearings, pacing, timing, and simple relocation drills near base.
Day 3: Follow bearings through mixed forest, identify prominent terrain features, and build route confidence in pairs.
Day 4: Plan a safe route using map, compass, GPS and smartphone cross-checks; estimate distance and travel time.
Day 5: Team-led navigation exercise over forest and meadow terrain with instructor observation and decision reviews.
Day 6: Final route-planning assessment, emergency navigation scenarios, debrief, and drop at Aut.

experiences.title: Buran Pass Trek
experiences.summary: A post-monsoon crossover trek from the Shimla side toward Kinnaur, shaped for fit trekkers who want forests, meadows, high-pass drama, and a clean route plan.
inclusions: Camping or local stay as per route
exclusions: Porter/mule for personal bag unless booked
itinerary: Day 1: Pickup from Shimla, drive to Janglik side, team briefing, document check, and overnight stay.
Day 2: Trek through village trails and forest sections toward the first meadow camp.
Day 3: Gradual ascent through open meadows, stream crossings, route briefings, and acclimatization pacing.
Day 4: Move toward high camp with weather review, pass-day briefing, and early rest.
Day 5: Cross Buran Pass with controlled pacing and descend toward the Kinnaur side.
Day 6: Trek toward Barua / exit village, transfer support, closing debrief, and rest.
Day 7: Buffer or return transfer to Shimla depending on road and weather conditions.

experiences.title: Kaktasar Trek
experiences.location: Great Himalayan National Park core zone
experiences.summary: A deeper GHNP core-zone trek starting and ending from the KEAS base, built for teams who want a longer, quieter, field-supported mountain route.
itinerary: Day 1: Aut pickup, KEAS base arrival, permit briefing, gear audit, and route overview.
Day 2: Trek from base into forest approach trails with movement discipline and ecology briefing.
Day 3: Continue through GHNP valley terrain, stream sections, and first remote camp setup.
Day 4: Gain altitude through mixed terrain; hydration, pacing, and weather checks through the day.
Day 5: Move toward Kaktasar approach zone with slower pacing and terrain-awareness drills.
Day 6: Exploration / objective day around Kaktasar side depending on weather and team condition.
Day 7: Begin return route with campsite clean-up and Leave No Trace audit.
Day 8: Descend through forest sections, local interpretation, and recovery camp.
Day 9: Trek back toward KEAS base, closing circle, and team debrief.
Day 10: Breakfast, contingency wrap-up, and drop at Aut.

experiences.title: Thinni Top Trek
experiences.summary: A compact Sainj Valley trek starting and ending from the KEAS base, ideal for first-timers, families, and groups wanting a gentler post-monsoon mountain route.
itinerary: Day 1: Aut pickup, KEAS base arrival, route briefing, gear check, and gentle acclimatization walk.
Day 2: Trek through Sainj Valley village and forest trails toward the first camp / stay.
Day 3: Ascend toward Thinni Top viewpoint with slow pacing, photography pauses, and field lunch.
Day 4: Descent via alternate forest route, recovery, local food, and closing debrief at base.
Day 5: Breakfast, optional short walk, and drop at Aut.

expeditions.title: Friendship Peak
expeditions.summary: A Manali-side snow objective for fit trekkers ready to progress into crampon movement, rope-team discipline, snow-slope judgement, and a guided summit attempt.
itinerary: Day 1: Arrive Manali, equipment audit, medical screening, and expedition briefing.
Day 2: Acclimatization hike toward Solang / Patalsu side and snow craft orientation.
Day 3: Trek to approach camp via Dhundi and Bakarthach meadows.
Day 4: Move to Lady Leg / advance base; crampon, ice axe, and rope-team practice.
Day 5: Summit attempt on Friendship Peak and return to base camp.
Day 6: Reserve weather day for summit or recovery.
Day 7: Descend to roadhead, debrief, certificate, and depart Manali.

expeditions.title: Pin Bhaba Pass
expeditions.summary: A dramatic crossover from the green Bhaba Valley to the stark Pin Valley, built around Kafnu approach days, meadow camps, moraine travel, pass-day pacing, and the exit to Mudh.
itinerary: Day 1: Shimla / Rampur transfer to Kafnu, permits, briefing, and gear check.
Day 2: Trek Kafnu to Mulling through forest, river sections, and meadow camps.
Day 3: Mulling to Kara with gradual altitude gain and stream crossings.
Day 4: Kara to Phustirang, pass briefing, early dinner, and weather review.
Day 5: Cross Pin Bhaba Pass and descend toward Mangrungse / Baldar terrain.
Day 6: Trek to Mudh village in Pin Valley and transfer toward Kaza.
Day 7: Buffer / road contingency day for weather, roadblocks, or acclimatization.

expeditions.title: Hanuman Tibba
expeditions.summary: A serious pyramid-shaped alpine objective north-west of Manali, suitable only for trained climbers with snow, ice, rope, camp discipline, and altitude experience.
itinerary: Day 1: Arrive Manali, document check, medical screen, and technical gear issue.
Day 2: Skills refresh: knots, fixed rope movement, cramponing, and crevasse response.
Day 3: Drive to Solang / Dhundi and trek toward Beas Kund base zone.
Day 4: Establish base camp, acclimatization walk, and load planning.
Day 5: Ferry load to Camp 1 and return for recovery.
Day 6: Move to Camp 1; snow anchors and route condition assessment.
Day 7: Establish higher camp depending on snow and weather.
Day 8: Summit attempt with alpine start and descent to lower camp.
Day 9: Reserve summit / weather day.
Day 10: Descend to base camp and clear route loads.
Day 11: Trek out to roadhead and transfer to Manali for debrief.

expeditions.title: Deo Tibba
expeditions.summary: A 6,001 m snow-dome objective above Jagatsukh that demands glacier travel, moraine negotiation, load-ferry planning, fixed-line judgement, and strong acclimatization.
packing: Harness and technical hardware as advised
Personal medical kit and hydration system
itinerary: Day 1: Arrive Manali, gear inspection, documentation, and expedition briefing.
Day 2: Acclimatization and technical refresh near Manali.
Day 3: Drive to Jagatsukh and trek to Chikka / Seri approach camp.
Day 4: Trek to Tenta / Deo Tibba base camp with gradual altitude gain.
Day 5: Load ferry and glacier travel practice.
Day 6: Establish advanced base camp; route opening and weather review.
Day 7: Move to summit camp depending on snow stability and team condition.
Day 8: Summit attempt on Deo Tibba and descend to safer camp.
Day 9: Reserve summit / weather day.
Day 10: Descend to base camp and clear all loads.
Day 11: Trek out to roadhead and return to Manali.

journalPosts.title: Why Sainj Valley works for slower, deeper adventure
journalPosts.excerpt: Sainj rewards travellers who want forests, village rhythm, GHNP ecozone access, and enough quiet to actually notice the landscape.
body: Sainj Valley is not designed for rushed checklist travel. That is exactly why it works for KEAS programs. The valley gives groups access to forest trails, village stays, rock craft, food systems, and slower conversations around ecology.

The operating advantage is rhythm. Groups can move in the morning, pause through the day, and use evenings for debrief, recovery, or community time. That makes Sainj especially strong for schools, creator retreats, WFH cohorts, and low-impact adventure programs.
KEAS treats Sainj as a base for learning and decompression rather than a backdrop. The route, stay, activity level, and cultural touchpoints are matched to the group.

journalPosts.title: How KEAS builds safety briefings into every route
journalPosts.excerpt: Good safety is not a paragraph in a brochure. It is a repeated habit before, during, and after every mountain day.
body: Every KEAS route starts with expectation-setting. We look at fitness, prior experience, weather, terrain, gear, road conditions, and the purpose of the group before finalising the day plan.

In the field, safety is communicated in simple language: what the terrain asks of you, where the hazards are, how the group will move, and what changes if conditions shift. This is especially important for rock craft, high passes, and expedition approaches.
Post-activity debriefs help guests understand their own decision-making, recovery needs, hydration, and readiness for the next day.

journalPosts.title: Designing Himalayan workations that still feel like travel
journalPosts.excerpt: A good workation protects work hours and travel energy. The trick is not doing everything; it is designing the day well.
body: Most workations fail when the itinerary ignores work. KEAS designs these programs around predictable work blocks, morning movement, evening recovery, and realistic expectations around connectivity.

A good day may include a short forest walk, a rock craft session, or a village experience before work begins. The afternoon stays protected, while evenings are used for decompression, food, or community time.
The goal is not to squeeze a vacation around calls. It is to create a mountain rhythm that lets people work clearly and still return home with a real sense of place.
